summary:
A public-facing web tool that turns SPHEREx spectral-image cutouts into a blink movie: you enter sky coordinates (RA/Dec), it queries NASA/IPAC IRSA for every SPHEREx epoch covering that position and animates them in time order, so moving objects (brown dwarfs, asteroids, high proper-motion stars) pop out exactly the way Pluto was discovered in 1930.

Preset high-proper-motion targets: Barnard's Star, WISE 0855, Epsilon Indi B, RW Aurigae
Difference mode (epoch N − epoch N−1): moving sources appear as dipole pairs
Crude spectrum (stretch goal): center-pixel flux vs wavelength across all 6 detector bandpasses
URL parameters: "?ra=&dec=&fov=&band=" — shareable/queryable links
Aladin Lite sky background + Gaia/WISE catalog overlay via the Aladin UI
details:
Detailed Information About the Project

1. What It Does & How It Works

  • Function: AZURA is a public-facing web tool designed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 ("Planet X and SPHEREx" challenge). It allows users to enter sky coordinates and transforms SPHEREx spectral-image cutouts into a dynamic "blink movie" (an animated time-lapse sequence).
  • How It Works: The backend is built with Python (Flask) alongside custom data-probing and query scripts (such as _probe_irsa.py) to fetch and process astronomical data from IRSA. The frontend uses vanilla HTML5 and JavaScript without heavy frameworks or build steps, keeping the architecture clean and lightweight.

2. Benefits and Intended Impact

  • Benefits: It simplifies complex and raw astronomical data, turning it into accessible, visual, and interactive animations that researchers, astronomers, and space enthusiasts can easily analyze.
  • Intended Impact: To provide an innovative solution for exploring the cosmos, making space science data more approachable, engaging, and digestible for both professionals and the general public.

3. Tools, Programming Languages, and Technologies Used

  • Programming Languages: Python (50.6%) and HTML/JavaScript (49.4%).
  • Frameworks & Software: Flask (web framework), _probe_irsa.py (IRSA data script), requirements.txt (dependency management), and render.yaml (deployment configuration).
  • Development & Organization: Managed via GitHub, featuring structured directories such as docs/, sprints/, static/, and data/cache/ to maintain clean sprint documentation and version control.

4. Creativity and Key Factors Considered

  • Creativity: It stands out as a focused solo project that leverages a minimalistic approach ("no build step, no framework") to solve a complex astrophysical data visualization challenge creatively.
    • Strict alignment with the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 theme ("Planet X and SPHEREx").
    • High performance and simplicity, avoiding unnecessary bloat or complex build configurations.
    • Detailed planning and progress tracking through sprint logs and structured codebase documentation.
